dpa.title: Data processing
dpa.heading: Data processing agreement
dpa.intro: This page documents every external service {app} auto-reply translation routes customer message data through, what it receives, and how to restrict cross-border transfer.
dpa.leavesBody: When an inbound WhatsApp message triggers a multilingual auto-reply, {app} may send the message body and the reply text to one or more of the following translation providers, depending on which drivers your administrator has activated.
dpa.residencyBody: Set a stricter routing mode for this workspace. Auto-reply translation will only route through providers compatible with the selected mode; the rest are silently skipped at runtime.
dpa.ownerOnly: Only the workspace owner can change this setting.
dpa.translationSettings: Change the routing mode in translation settings

any.name: No restriction
any.text: Use whichever active provider the fallback chain picks. Best uptime, no compliance restrictions.

eu_only.name: EU-only routing
eu_only.text: Only DeepL (Germany) and self-hosted LibreTranslate are allowed. Compatible with GDPR Article 44 cross-border transfer rules.

local.name: On-premise only
local.text: Only the self-hosted LibreTranslate driver is allowed. Customer message text never leaves your own server. Requires LibreTranslate to be configured.

dpa.retentionBody: Translated phrases are cached for 24 hours on this {app} install. After that the cache entry expires and the next request re-routes through the active provider. Translation API providers themselves may retain logs per their own DPAs; see the linked policies above.
dpa.erasureBody: {app} stores translated reply variants alongside each auto-reply rule in your database. Deleting a contact or workspace via the standard delete flows removes their conversation history; cached translations are not personally identifiable as they are keyed by phrase, not by contact.
